rag.name: MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap_of_hasCompactSupport
rag.content:
/-- A version of *Fubini theorem* for continuous functions with compact support: one may swap
the order of integration with respect to locally finite measures. One does not assume that the
measures are σ-finite, contrary to the usual Fubini theorem. -/
lemma integral_integral_swap_of_hasCompactSupport
    {f : X → Y → E} (hf : Continuous f.uncurry) (h'f : HasCompactSupport f.uncurry)
    {μ : Measure X} {ν : Measure Y} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ] [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν] :
    ∫ x, (∫ y, f x y ∂ν) ∂μ = ∫ y, (∫ x, f x y ∂μ) ∂ν := by
  let U := Prod.fst '' (tsupport f.uncurry)
  have : Fact (μ U < ∞) := ⟨(IsCompact.image h'f continuous_fst).measure_lt_top⟩
  let V := Prod.snd '' (tsupport f.uncurry)
  have : Fact (ν V < ∞) := ⟨(IsCompact.image h'f continuous_snd).measure_lt_top⟩
  calc
  ∫ x, (∫ y, f x y ∂ν) ∂μ = ∫ x, (∫ y in V, f x y ∂ν) ∂μ := by
    congr 1 with x
    apply (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero (fun y hy ↦ ?_)).symm
    contrapose! hy
    have : (x, y) ∈ Function.support f.uncurry := hy
    exact mem_image_of_mem _ (subset_tsupport _ this)
  _ = ∫ x in U, (∫ y in V, f x y ∂ν) ∂μ := by
    apply (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero (fun x hx ↦ ?_)).symm
    have : ∀ y, f x y = 0 := by
      intro y
      contrapose! hx
      have : (x, y) ∈ Function.support f.uncurry := hx
      exact mem_image_of_mem _ (subset_tsupport _ this)
    simp [this]
  _ = ∫ y in V, (∫ x in U, f x y ∂μ) ∂ν := by
    apply integral_integral_swap
    apply (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset (subset_tsupport f.uncurry)).mp
    refine ⟨(h'f.stronglyMeasurable_of_prod hf).aestronglyMeasurable, ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ : ∃ C, ∀ p, ‖f.uncurry p‖ ≤ C := hf.bounded_above_of_compact_support h'f
    exact hasFiniteIntegral_of_bounded (C := C) (Eventually.of_forall hC)
  _ = ∫ y, (∫ x in U, f x y ∂μ) ∂ν := by
    apply setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero (fun y hy ↦ ?_)
    have : ∀ x, f x y = 0 := by
      intro x
      contrapose! hy
      have : (x, y) ∈ Function.support f.uncurry := hy
      exact mem_image_of_mem _ (subset_tsupport _ this)
    simp [this]
  _ = ∫ y, (∫ x, f x y ∂μ) ∂ν := by
    congr 1 with y
    apply setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero (fun x hx ↦ ?_)
    contrapose! hx
    have : (x, y) ∈ Function.support f.uncurry := hx
    exact mem_image_of_mem _ (subset_tsupport _ this)

C0_dependencies.name: MeasureTheory.BoundedCompactSupport.finset_sum
C0_dependencies.content:
/-- A finite sum of bounded compactly supported functions is bounded compactly supported. -/
theorem finset_sum
    (hF : ∀ i ∈ s, BoundedCompactSupport (F i)) :
    BoundedCompactSupport (fun x ↦ ∑ i ∈ s, F i x) := by
  classical
  induction s using Finset.induction with
  | empty => simp [BoundedCompactSupport.zero]
  | @insert j s hjs IH =>
    simp_rw [Finset.sum_insert hjs]
    apply BoundedCompactSupport.add
    · exact hF _ (Finset.mem_insert_self j s)
    · exact IH (fun i hi ↦ hF _ (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hi))

theorem lintegral_tsum [Countable β] {f : β → α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (f i) μ) :
    ∫⁻ a, ∑' i, f i a ∂μ = ∑' i, ∫⁻ a, f i a ∂μ := by
  classical
  simp only [ENNReal.tsum_eq_iSup_sum]
  rw [lintegral_iSup_directed]
  · simp [lintegral_finset_sum' _ fun i _ => hf i]
  · intro b
    exact Finset.aemeasurable_sum _ fun i _ => hf i
  · intro s t
    use s ∪ t
    constructor
    · exact fun a => Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset Finset.subset_union_left
    · exact fun a => Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset Finset.subset_union_right

    (insert : ∀ ⦃a : α⦄ {s : Finset α}, a ∉ s → p s → p (insert a s)) : ∀ s, p s :=
  cons_induction empty fun a s ha => (s.cons_eq_insert a ha).symm ▸ insert ha

informal_statement: For any function \( f : \beta \rightarrow \alpha \) in a seminormed abelian group \( \alpha \), the range of \( f \) is bounded if and only if there exists a constant \( C \) such that the norm of \( f(x) \) is less than or equal to \( C \) for all \( x \).
informal_proof:
The proof of this statement is straightforward and relies on the definition of boundedness in a seminormed abelian group.

First, recall that a set is bounded if it is contained within a ball of finite radius. In this context, the range of \( f \) being bounded means there exists some constant \( C \) such that for all \( x \) in the domain of \( f \), the norm of \( f(x) \) does not exceed \( C \). This directly aligns with the statement that there exists a constant \( C \) such that \( \|f(x)\| \leq C \) for all \( x \).

The proof uses a conversion tactic to relate the given theorem to an existing definition or lemma, and then simplifies the goal to match this relationship. Essentially, the equivalence follows directly from the definitions of boundedness and the properties of norms in a seminormed space.

Thus, the proof confirms that the boundedness of the range of \( f \) is equivalent to the existence of such a constant \( C \) that bounds the norms of all elements in the range.
